name: Census Bureau Building Permits Survey (BPS) — county-level new housing permits
measures: Number and valuation of new privately-owned housing units authorized by building permits, by permitting jurisdiction.
granularity: county-level files exist, but only a subset of jurisdictions (roughly half) are surveyed monthly — the rest report annually — so a county-monthly series has real gaps; clean county-level time series are built from the annual files, not the monthly ones
update_frequency: monthly (preliminary ~12th workday, revised ~18th workday) for the subset surveyed monthly; annual for the rest, with final annual data published the following May
history: county-level annual files available for many years; monthly county coverage is partial

access.api_key_required: unclear — the national/regional/state series is exposed via the Census timeseries API (api.census.gov/data/timeseries/eits/bps), but county-level geography was not confirmed to be available through that same API in this research pass
access.method: county-level files are published as downloadable ASCII/comma-delimited files on census.gov/construction/bps; the FAQ directs people to call or email the Census Residential Construction Branch for some geography/format combinations, which suggests the clean self-serve path isn't fully documented

license: US federal government work; public domain by default, no login or paid tier found.
fits_gap: Would be a national analog to the NYC-only Housing Database / rezonings sources backing the 'development' pillar (pipeline_units_pct, new_units_5y_pct in neighborhood.py), which is needed for the stated US-wide generalization goal.

correlation.note: Not evaluated quantitatively; app/research/evaluate_series.py doesn't exist yet.

recommendation_rationale: The underlying idea (a national permits series for the development pillar) is sound and the data is free and public-domain, but this research pass could not confirm a clean, documented, no-key programmatic path to county-level monthly data — the authoritative county files appear to require pulling annual ASCII/CSV releases (with real monthly-coverage gaps) rather than a tidy API call. Worth a second, deeper look specifically at whether api.census.gov's timeseries/eits/bps endpoint (or the County Business Patterns / SOCDS mirrors) exposes county geography before committing engineering time — don't implement on the strength of this pass alone.
